- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.6) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) or volatile, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction to pessimism.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in the next 5–10 days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% to prevent overcorrection.
- Model shows persistent mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days are below 65–68, forecast tends to be too low; adjust upward by 1–2% to reflect reversion to prior mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) price action; weight recent sentiment and price data more heavily in final 10–15 days of forecast.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.6), model tends to err on the side of caution; increase forecast slightly to reflect latent bullishness unless strong bearish signals persist.
